title: Goat Maps — Dragon's Back Race 2027 unofficial stage guide, cutoffs, entry and support rules
publisher: Goat Maps (unofficial third-party guide, compiled from organiser-published information)
claims: The 2027 edition runs 6-11 September 2027, with registration in Conwy on Sunday 5 September; Dragon's Fire runs 6-7 September and Dragon's Tail 10-11 September.

Compiled stage distances and ascent: Day 1 Conwy Castle to Nant Gwynant 50 km / 4,100 m; Day 2 Nant Gwynant to Dolgellau 60 km / 3,200 m; Day 3 Dolgellau to Ceredigion 66 km / 2,900 m; Day 4 through the Elan Valley 67 km / 1,900 m; Day 5 into the Bannau Brycheiniog 75 km / 3,200 m; Day 6 to Cardiff 65 km / 1,300 m. Each day starts 06:00 and the course closes at 22:00, a 16-hour window.

Compiled in-day cutoffs include Day 1 Ogwen Valley aid station 29 km 14:00, Pen-y-Pass water point 37 km 16:40, Pyg Track junction 18:30; Day 2 Cwm Bychan 37 km 15:45; Day 3 Machynlleth 40 km 16:15; Day 4 Elan Village 33 km 14:30 and a later water point 19:00; Day 5 Cray Reservoir 43 km 14:45; Day 6 Trelewis 34 km 14:00.

The full race and Hatchling cost £2,095 with a £400 deposit followed by monthly payments; Dragon's Fire £599, Dragon's Tail £399; minimum age over 20; there is no qualifying race, entrants accept a participant declaration.

There is no crewing: supporters cannot run with runners, carry anything or hand over food, and cannot enter camps, aid stations or water points; they can see runners off at Conwy Castle and meet them at the finish in Cardiff; followers use live GPS tracking and Dragon Mail; buying food from public shops and cafés on the route is allowed.

Mandatory carry each day: waterproof jacket or smock, waterproof trousers, survival bag, synthetic warm layer of at least 300 g, baseplate compass, headtorch, red rear light, bottles or bladder holding 1.5 L, and a phone; the race provides a GPS tracker and a map.

Runners sleep in eight-person basic tents with portable toilets and no showers, bringing their own sleeping bag and mat; one Ortlieb 59 L dry bag (15 kg limit) is moved to each camp, and a 10 L resupply bag up to 2.5 kg waits at each day's aid station.

Trekking poles are allowed except on the Day 1 Tryfan and Crib Goch scrambles, where poles must be stowed; phone signal is not reliable on the remote route and the day's line must be downloaded offline before leaving camp.

Registration is Sunday 5 September, 13:00-17:00 at Ysgol Porth Y Felin in Conwy, with a compulsory 17:30 briefing; Conwy has a station on the North Wales Coast Line and is about 1.5 hours' drive from Manchester and Liverpool airports; coaches between Cardiff and Conwy and the 23 kg transfer bag are paid extras booked ahead.
The guide quotes Capel Curig September averages of 16.0 °C high, 9.4 °C low and 206 mm of rain over about 16 days.
